evidence: The pooled ring removal bins |Q| from 1.5 to 10.5 Å⁻¹ whatever the volume holds (RingParams.q_min, q_max: src/nebula3d/_ringplane.py:59-60), and its detector, _detect_rings (src/nebula3d/preprocessing/radial_background.py:1321), took the noise its candidates must rise pooled_min_snr = 6 times (_ringplane.py:101), 1.4826·median(|diff(g − rough)|)/√2, over every bin (radial_background.py:1364). The bins no plane samples (NaN in the pooled profile) are filled by _fill_nan_1d, edge-extended, so flat past the last measured bin (:1309-1318, :1348), the sparse ones interpolated across (:1352-1357), and SNIP (:1358) leaves a flat run as it is: there g − rough is exactly 0. On a volume whose counts end well inside 10.5 Å⁻¹, once about half the differences were 0 the noise was 0, the 6σ floor went, and every local maximum became a candidate. The candidates above the noise are kept out of the judged shells' flanks (src/nebula3d/preprocessing/pooled_rings.py:560-566; src/nebula3d/preprocessing/ring_isotropy.py:309-311), so a real ring's isotropy test drew its line through two or three flank bins (a signal-to-noise of about 1e14 to 1e16) and skipped its curve check, which needs four (ring_isotropy.py:454). Measured on 39b0835 (synthetic volumes only): of the validation's dev cases, whose box reaches 6.44 Å⁻¹ at its faces and 11.16 Å⁻¹ at its corners, only dev-coverage ends inside the range (counts cut at 4.511 Å⁻¹, no ring). At n=161, 151 of its 224 bins are empty, the noise is 0 (0.0074 over the measured bins), 24 candidates, 18 judged and rejected as the crystal's own, none subtracted. At n=81, 77 of 112 bins are empty and its 10 candidates are all listed in the coarse-grid notice (G1), whose remedy, pooled_confirm_rings=False, subtracted all ten as rings (1.70 to 3.96 Å⁻¹, 9.4 % of |I|). The dev crystal at n=161 with no counts past 4 Å⁻¹ and rings planted at 2.2 and 3.3 Å⁻¹: candidates at 2.00 and 2.41 Å⁻¹ left the 2.2 ring a signal-to-noise of 9.9e15 and no curve check. Against where its counts end, the dev crystal's noise at n=161 is 0 from 4 to 5.5 Å⁻¹, 0.04 of the measured noise at 6 to 6.5, 0.28 at 7, 0.45 at 7.5, 0.60 at 8, 0.73 at 9 and 0.90 at 10.
proposed_fix: (b) The noise from the measured bins only: _measured_noise takes the MAD of the residual's bin-to-bin differences, /√2, over the pairs of adjacent bins that are both measured (finite in the pooled profile, and not sparse: sampled by a tenth of the median number of planes or more), and is inf with no such pair, so nothing then passes the floor. With every bin measured it is the estimate over all the bins, as before. Weighed and left out: (c), a ring judged only on two flank bins a side or more, else not judged, with a retry that keeps out the confirmed rings alone, which never fired with (b) in place; docs/pipeline.md keeps it as an option. With (b) a weak ring beside a strong one can fall under the 6σ cut and drop out of the keep-outs, which used the same cut: left in the strong ring's flank it lifts the flank line and can fail a real ring (the demo of tests/test_demo.py, below). (A) The shells kept out of the flanks of those judged are picked at half the detection cut, 3σ (pooled_rings._KEEP_OUT_SNR_SHARE), while detection and the Al-line route stay at 6σ: a keep-out only protects a flank and is never subtracted, so the lower bar is the cautious side. IsotropyConfig.min_cells is not changed (the open question in the note).

note: Approved by the manager on the user's delegation: fix (b) on 2026-10-19, as a freeze blocker, and the keep-outs at 3σ (option A) on 2026-10-24, because a keep-out only protects a flank, so the lower bar is the cautious side. Implemented by fb3832d (b) and ca1803a (A). Against main (7882fc7, and 39b0835 before it), on the final code: every dev case's ring-removed volume at n=81 and n=161 is bit-identical (16 of 16, dev-coverage's too: with pooled_confirm_rings on, its flood was rejected or left unconfirmed, never subtracted), and so is the console's demo volume's at 161³ (and at 61³). Their ring diagnostics change in two ways: dev-coverage's flood is gone (no candidate at either grid, no coarse-grid notice, the remedy subtracting nothing), and on dev-rings and dev-rings-shell at n=161 the 3σ keep-outs add bumps of the crystal's own near the 2.2 Å⁻¹ ring, which is then judged on fewer flank bins (dev-rings: signal-to-noise 47.6 for 35.5, the curve check skipped; dev-rings-shell: 22.5 for 37.6, curve 1.06), still a ring. The 97-point demo of tests/test_demo.py (±3 r.l.u., counts ending at 7.55 Å⁻¹, its old noise 0.37 of the measured) reaches the bug: main subtracted 7 shells, the aluminium rings at 2.69, 3.11, 4.38, 5.12 and 6.76 Å⁻¹ and the weak 222 and 420 lines at 5.36 and 6.95 Å⁻¹ (17.6 % of |I|); now the five (14.1 %). With (b) alone the 420, under 6σ, sat in the 331's flank and failed it (signal-to-noise 1.3, curve −0.29), and the punch took the 331 left in for a Bragg peak at (2.81, 3, 1.88); with (A) it is kept out and the 331 is confirmed (33.7). Arm A on dev re-run on the final code: 32 of 32 entries identical, 5 of 8 cases pass, as recorded; 18 of its 24 run logs unchanged, dev-coverage's three differing in the ring line alone (no_confirmed_rings with 18 shells not confirmed, now no_rings with none) and dev-rings's three in the flatten's R² (-0.000, now 0.000), which main's a2706f2 changed, not this finding. On 39b0835, 5 of the first 7 new tests fail (the other two pin _measured_noise itself); the two keep-out tests and test_demo fail with (b) alone, and the weak-neighbour test on main too (main subtracted the 420). On volumes constructed with their counts cut short, (b) cut the candidates from 14–37 to 0–6, removed every false shell the flood made, and judged strong rings on two flank bins a side (signal-to-noise 37 to 64, curve 0.92 to 1.05); weak rings under the restored 6σ go undetected, as on full coverage. Left: (c) is an option not taken (docs/pipeline.md). Outside this finding, a known limit: a weak ring (amplitude 0.05 beside one of 0.5) is subtracted at 1.2 to 2.4 times its amplitude in every geometry tried, full coverage included. Open for the user: between a box's face and its corner a shell is measured in some directions only, and the isotropy test judges it on 16 to 32 of its 128 direction cells (IsotropyConfig.min_cells is 16); on a synthetic cubic crystal, shells of the crystal's own pass there as rings whatever the noise (4.41 Å⁻¹ on a ±3 Å⁻¹ box; 5.01, 5.49, 7.29 and 9.01 Å⁻¹ on others). min_cells = 64, half the sphere, with (b) removes all of them, keeps every planted ring and leaves the dev cases identical, but whether a ring may be confirmed from part of the sphere, and from how much of it, is the user's rule, so min_cells is unchanged.

decision.by: the manager, on the user's delegation
decision.option: the noise estimate over measured, non-sparse adjacent bins (fix b, 2026-10-19), with the keep-outs picked at half the detection cut, 3σ, because a keep-out only protects a flank, so the lower bar is the cautious side (option A, 2026-10-24)
